title: Intro: Redwood x CobaltGrid - Partnership & Integration Scope
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and CobaltGrid to explore a go-to-market integration and technical compatibility for hosting Redwood Dedicated on CobaltGrid's managed GPU fabric. High-level alignment on marketplace listing, certificate/KMS integration, VPC peering options, and a mutual pilot with Ampere-based instances. Action items and SE deep-dive scheduled.
next_steps: Redwood to send partner integration checklist and API endpoint table
Schedule SE deep-dive to validate instance compatibility and perf expectations (target 2025-07-16)
CobaltGrid to provide test VPC creds and sample AMI/container images
Exchange SOC2 / security pack and a proposed NDA for marketplace listing
action_items: Sofia Patel: Send partner checklist, pricing model snapshot, and Redwood partner deck by 2025-07-11
Liam O'Connor: Run initial compatibility check against CobaltGrid Ampere A800 and GA100 fleets and share notes by 2025-07-16
Ethan Park: Provide test VPC peering info and a small test account (bootstrap) by 2025-07-12
Marta Ruiz: Share CobaltGrid marketplace requirements and revenue-share baseline by 2025-07-14
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CobaltGrid Head of Partnerships), Ethan Park (CobaltGrid Cloud Architect), Nadia Chen (BD), Kenji Ito (Infra Lead)

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see folks are on, I'm Sofia with Redwood Inference, AE for the partnerships team. Louie? Liam? can you -
[00:08] Liam O'Connor: Yeah hi all, Liam SE here, I'll be doing the technical side. Excited to go through what CobaltGrid has and how we could integrate Redwood Dedicated.
[00:15] Marta Ruiz: Great, hi hi. We have a quick agenda - partnership scope, technical fit (GPU types, networking), and go-to-market. Is that right Sofia?
[00:24] Sofia Patel: Yep, that sounds good. Also we want to surface any security or compliance blockers early.
[00:30] Ethan Park: Perfect. From our side I run the cloud infra for CobaltGrid, we operate a managed GPU fabric - mix of Ampere and older NVIDIA GA100 nodes. We also have a managed marketplace for third-party services.
[00:43] Sofia Patel: Nice. Maybe start with a quick overview of what a partnership with Redwood typically looks like? And then Liam can ask about the infra specifics.
[00:51] Liam O'Connor: Sure. Quick primer: Redwood Dedicated is a reserved, customer-isolated serving tier—think dedicated GPU pools with capacity that can be co-located in partner data centers or on partner-managed cloud. We provide the same API surface as our hosted API, plus tooling for rollouts, tracing, and token-level cost analysis.
[01:10] Marta Ruiz: OK so you want us to host? Or this is a managed service you put on top of CobaltGrid?
[01:17] Sofia Patel: It's flexible. There are a few models: 1) Redwood runs on your managed instances as a partner-managed offering, 2) We support a marketplace listing where customers can deploy Redwood Dedicated onto CobaltGrid with billing through your platform, or 3) Full private deployment where the customer runs Redwood internally but uses CobaltGrid for GPUs.
[01:37] Kenji Ito: For marketplace listing we'd need to understand the network topology—VPC peering or private link? We prefer private link for multi-tenant customers.
[01:45] Ethan Park: And also KMS integration. We require key management via our HSM for anything that handles customer keys.
[01:51] Liam O'Connor: Understood. Redwood supports external KMS via standard KMIP or cloud KMS APIs; we also support customer-managed keys for dedicated/private deployments. Key rotation is automated but we can map to your HSM schedule.
[02:05] Nadia Chen: Are there limits on model size or perf differences when you run on Ampere vs Nvidia?
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: Good question. There are perf deltas. Ampere ones like the A800 are very cost-effective for many quantized models; GA100/like A100 have better FP16 throughput for largest models. We often recommend quantized 4/8-bit backends where possible to save cost. We'll run benchmarks in the initial pilot to set expectations.
[02:33] Marta Ruiz: What about latency? Our customers expect sub-100ms for 256-token responses for some use cases.
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: Sub-100ms at 256 tokens is achievable for smaller models—we'll need to validate with your instance sizes and networking topology. Latency is influenced by batching, KV cache hits, and kernel choices—some of which are runtime-configurable.
[02:56] Sofia Patel: To ground this in a pilot scope, how about we outline a 4-week pilot where Redwood runs inference against a CobaltGrid Ampere pool with a small, representative prompt set, and we measure throughput/latency/token-cost?
[03:09] Ethan Park: Sounds good. We can provision a test VPC and a limited fleet.
[03:14] Kenji Ito: Quick Q on tenancy: do you need dedicated tenancy at the host level or can you run multi-tenant with strong isolation?
[03:21] Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated, we expect dedicated GPU nodes per customer. For marketplace deployments we can support multi-tenant control plane with isolated runtime instances, but the most robust path is node-level isolation.
[03:33] Marta Ruiz: On go-to-market, what does Redwood expect from partners? Co-marketing spend? Revenue share?
[03:40] Sofia Patel: We have a partner program that includes joint listing, co-sourced leads, and a revenue share that varies by commitment. For early integrations we waive some fees to incentivize pilots—this is all flexible and we can share the partner T&C doc.
[03:53] Nadia Chen: Are there references or other partners who've done this?
[03:57] Sofia Patel: Yes, we've worked with several cloud partners and SI firms. I'll include a short list and case study links in follow-up.
[04:04] [04:04] (brief cross-talk as someone joins with audio echo)
[04:20] Liam O'Connor: Back to technical: on images we support both containerized inference images and AMI-like instances. For managed partners we usually provide a container and an orchestrator that can be deployed in Kubernetes or on your VM fleet.
[04:35] Ethan Park: We use a mix—K8s for orchestration for most tenant workloads, but some customers prefer bare-metal VMs with GPU passthrough.
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: We can support either. There are kernel-level optimizations and we may need to tune drivers and CUDA/cuDNN versions. We'll share a compatibility matrix.
[04:54] Marta Ruiz: About security: SOC2 and ISO—do you have those? Our compliance team will ask.
[04:59] Sofia Patel: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll attach the security pack and an architecture diagram. For marketplace listing we can surface our attestation.
[05:08] Ethan Park: Great. Also data residency—some of our customers are EEA only. Is there support for region locking?
[05:15] Sofia Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported with private deployments or dedicated pools in specific regions. That's common.
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: On telemetry and observability—our runtime emits token-level latency and cost logs, plus traces. If you want ingestion into your observability, we can push to a partner endpoint or expose a pull API.
[05:34] Kenji Ito: We would like logs to go to our Splunk with restricted PII redaction. We need a schema for what you emit.
[05:42] Liam O'Connor: We'll share the schema. Redaction rules can be applied on our side before shipping logs if needed.
[05:49] Marta Ruiz: How about billing integration? If we do marketplace billing, customers pay through you or through us?
[05:56] Sofia Patel: Two models: direct billing through Redwood with partner referral credit, or billing via your marketplace with revenue share and settlement. We'll need legal to look at settlement cadence.
[06:07] Nadia Chen: Any upfront commitments required from partners?
[06:10] Sofia Patel: For Dedicated, often a modest commit for reserved capacity is common. For marketplace things are more flexible initially. We'll propose a pilot-first approach.
[06:19] Ethan Park: For the pilot, what's needed from our infra team?
[06:23] Liam O'Connor: Test VPC, credentials for a bootstrap user (least privilege), a short list of prompt templates and sample models to run, and traceroute/latency checks. We can provide a small harness to run evals.
[06:34] Kenji Ito: We can do that. Also we need to understand the footprint—how many GPUs will you need for a small pilot?
[06:40] Liam O'Connor: Depends on throughput. For initial perf tests a pod of 4-8 Ampere GPUs should be sufficient to validate latency and cost curves. We'll give a recommended minimum after we see your fleet sizes.
[06:51] [06:51] (brief pause)
[07:05] Marta Ruiz: On legal/compliance, our procurement team will need redwood's certs and possibly an NDA.
[07:12] Sofia Patel: We'll send standard NDA and the SOC2 pack. Also we have a marketplace agreement template.
[07:18] Nadia Chen: Any blockers on support SLAs? Our customers will want 99.9 uptime for production.
[07:25] Sofia Patel: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime depending on commitment. We'll outline SLA tiers in the partner doc.
[07:31] Liam O'Connor: One technical risk I want to note: model quantization compatibility. If you force 4-bit quantization on some model variants there can be quality regressions; we recommend running a quality eval to quantify this up front.
[07:46] Ethan Park: Understood. We'll provide a small eval suite.
[07:50] Sofia Patel: Great. Anything else we should capture now?
[07:54] Kenji Ito: A question about kernel-level ops—do you use Triton or a custom runtime?
[07:59] Liam O'Connor: We use a custom high-throughput runtime optimized for attention kernels, but we can plug into Triton-compatible execution paths for certain stacks. We'll document runtime dependencies.
[08:13] Marta Ruiz: On marketing—what assets do you expect from us for the marketplace listing? Logos, product description, and security attestations?
[08:20] Sofia Patel: Yes, logos, a 1-paragraph about the integration, and contact for co-marketing. We'll draft the listing copy and share.
[08:27] Nadia Chen: Can Redwood support a joint webinar?
[08:30] Sofia Patel: Absolutely, those are core to our partner program. We can co-present a tech/developer focused webinar.
[08:36] [08:36] (laughter)
[08:45] Liam O'Connor: Next steps recap—SE deep dive to validate instances and perf on 7/16, partner checklist share by Redwood 7/11, CobaltGrid to provide test VPC by 7/12. Does that align?
[08:57] Marta Ruiz: Yes. We'll also send marketplace requirements by 7/14.
[09:02] Sofia Patel: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the 7/16 slot and include the partner deck and security pack.
[09:08] Kenji Ito: One last note—network egress costs. If you run many token-heavy workloads, we need to model egress.
[09:15] Liam O'Connor: We'll capture egress in the cost model and include it in the pilot metrics.
[09:21] Sofia Patel: Awesome. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs and next steps.
[09:25] Marta Ruiz: Thanks.
[09:27] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., "Red wood"), some overlapping speech at 04:04 mark, and a few incomplete sentences typical of an automated transcription. Shared artifacts: partner deck link (internal): https://redwood.com/decks/partner-onboarding (doc), pilot harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/partner-pilot (repo), security pack: https://redwood.com/security/soc2-2024.pdf
